To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
catalytic inhibition of GBA by CBE increases α-synucleins, while RNA interference of GBA 1 reduces α-synucleines.
GBA RNAi but not conduritol-β epoxide increases levels of α-synucleinin SH-SY5 cells.
RNA interference towards Gba1 and catalytic inactivation of glucocerebroside activity have different effects on the levels of α-synucleins in cellular models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of catalytic inhibition of GBA and RNAi towards GBA on α-syn levels in cellular models.
the effects of glucocerebroside deficiency on α-syn levels in cellular models of Parkinson's disease.
the effects of GBA 1 RNA interference and catalytic inhibition on α-synuclein levels in cellular models.

GBA RNAi but not Conduritol-ß-epoxide increases α-synucleins levels in SH-SY 5Y cells.
catalytic inhibition of GBA 1 increases α-synucleintotal levels while GBA RNAi decreases α-synucleintonic levels.
GBA 1 activity is not involved in the regulation of total α-syuclein levels in the cell.

catalytic inhibition of GBA increases total α-syn level in both cell types, while RNAi of GBA does not.

catalytic inhibition of the glucocerebroside enzyme with Conduritol-beta epoxide does not increase levels of total alpha-synuclein.
